findings.reason: the missing-arm case is the most likely one at landing (a run whose manifest records no arm at all) and nothing else in the plan requires it.
findings.text: §17's deliverable names three conditions under which the landing measures the arm itself (a recorded arm that is missing, recorded at another revision, or ran another command), but its done-when plants only a superseded head, a differing command and a matching arm, so a node that measures for the revision and command mismatches and still refuses on a missing arm passes the whole gate with one third of its deliverable unimplemented

findings.reason: without a measured lock-held case the retry is optional work, and without a stated bound the worker has to invent the budget the gate will accept.
findings.text: §18's deliverable requires that when `extensions.worktreeConfig` must be written and the configuration lock is held, creation "retries for a bounded time before refusing", but the done-when exercises only the already-true case, the absent-setting case with no lock, and `core.checkStat`, so a node that keeps the present single attempt and refuses immediately passes; the deliverable also states no bound, so even a test written for it could assert nothing about the wait

findings.reason: either the clause moves to §9 in s2's text or s2 stays implementable until the counts are recorded; as written, a reader computing impl from the declarations believes the sweep was measured when no count exists anywhere.
findings.text: `plan-section-declarations` now marks s2 `done`, while s2's own done-when (plan.html:57) still requires that "the coordinator runs the sweep on the live crew home and records the count of identity files before and after in this plan's evidence record", and the s2 landing comment (plan.html:163-165) says that sweep is deferred to §9; `docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html` carries no before/after count, so the section is declared complete over an unperformed clause of its own gate

findings.reason: the followup is the coordinator's next action, and this is the same gap that was raised for f-wftl-001 and answered by a followup naming every unbuilt section.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py`, `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py` and `reckon/crew/routing.py` all exist; `routing.py:2380` writes `extensions.worktreeConfig true` unconditionally on every creation, so s18's cited root cause resolves; s12's premise holds, since `dispatch_batch.py` carries no `allow_unreviewed_plan` field while `dispatch.py` does (line 1244).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s17's gate never plants a missing arm and s18's gate never exercises the bounded retry, so each leaves half of its own deliverable unmeasured; s12's done-when, as revised, does hold its certificate against the batch path.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate writes a repository test and a log on disk, §9's record lives at `docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html`, and that file exists with the `s2-identity-published-with-its-claim` anchor the s2 landing comment cites.

rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each stated root cause matches the cited evidence, and each endpoint is reachable and checkable; s2's declaration-versus-done-when mismatch is raised under done_when rather than as a reasoning defect.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s12 (batch waiver), s17 (landing measures a mismatched arm) and s18 (worktree creation leaves the shared config alone) each name one deliverable; s18's retry is the same goal's contention case, not a second one.
